The first full release of ProDHCPServer: a portable DHCP server for Windows 10/11, built for AV field technicians. Plug your laptop into a device, press **Start**, and see within seconds whether it got an IP address, with a plain-English reason and next step if it didn't. Press **Stop** and your laptop's network settings go back exactly as they were.

All three phases passed hands-on testing with real AV equipment in October 2026.

## Download

1. Download `ProDHCPServer-v1.0.0-win-x64.exe` below. It's a single file: nothing to install, no .NET runtime needed.
2. Double-click it. Windows asks for administrator rights, because changing adapter settings and serving DHCP need them.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The exe isn't code-signed yet.** The first time you run it, Windows SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC": click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. On IT-managed work laptops, Microsoft Defender's attack surface reduction rules may block it outright. Run it on an unmanaged laptop, or ask IT to allow a fixed folder (for example `C:\Tools\ProDHCPServer\`).

To check the download wasn't corrupted, compare its SHA-256 with the `.sha256` file below. In PowerShell: `Get-FileHash .\ProDHCPServer-v1.0.0-win-x64.exe`

## What it does

**Core loop**
- Pick your Ethernet adapter; its settings are backed up before anything changes and restored on Stop, on exit, at shutdown, and after a crash.
- Eight-step status panel (adapter, link, static IP, DHCP server, DHCP traffic, lease, ping, WebUI), each green, amber or red with a reason and a suggested next step.
- Refuses to start if another DHCP server is already on the cable, so it won't fight a venue network.
- Device card with IP, MAC, manufacturer (offline lookup), and one-click **Open WebUI**.
- Warns about Wi-Fi or VPN on the same subnet, and about USB Ethernet adapters that have quietly stopped receiving (including old Realtek drivers).

**Visibility**
- Live ping graph for every device, with average, min, max and loss.
- Session log you can filter and export as text or CSV.
- Profiles for subnet, pool, lease time and DHCP options (gateway, DNS, NTP, options 43, 66, 150 and custom), with presets built from manufacturers' own documentation for Q-SYS, Biamp, Shure, Crestron, Extron, Lightware, Cisco and Poly gear and more.

**Discovery**
- **Found on the network** lists devices with a static IP, even on another subnet.
- **Reach it** adds a temporary address on the device's subnet so you can open its WebUI without stopping the server; it's removed on Stop like every other change.
- **Scan for static IPs** for quiet devices, covering your subnet and the common factory subnets.
- Read-only discovery over mDNS, SSDP/UPnP, PJLink, Art-Net, AES67 (SAP) and AMX, Q-SYS and Shure discovery.
- With [Npcap](https://npcap.com) installed, shows which switch, port and VLAN you're plugged into (LLDP/CDP).

## Known limits

- PJLink discovery hasn't been tried on a real projector yet.
- AV-over-IP multicast (Extron NAV, Dante video, SDVoE) on an unmanaged switch makes pings jump to hundreds of milliseconds. That's the network, not the app: use a managed switch with IGMP snooping.

Found a problem on site? [Open an issue](https://github.com/cookingwithsimon/ProDHCPServer/issues/new/choose) with the **Problem on site** form and include the session log.
